subject: english
chapter_title: The Proposal: A Farce in One Act

concepts.title: Lomov's Visit and the Marriage Proposal
concepts.definition: Ivan Vassilevitch Lomov, a wealthy neighbour with palpitations and nerves, calls on Stepan Stepanovitch Chubukov to ask for the hand of his daughter Natalya, but hesitates and circles around the point of the proposal.
concepts.key_idea: Lomov is thirty-five and must marry soon; his nerves and heart trouble make him a comic figure even as he tries to speak seriously.

solution_steps.explain: Lomov arrives in formal dress despite evening wear not being needed, signalling the formality of his purpose.
He drifts into courtesies and references instead of stating the proposal, betraying his nervousness.
At thirty-five he feels it is time to lead a quiet and regular life with a wife.

concepts.title: The Quarrel over Oxen Meadows
concepts.definition: While gathering courage to propose, Lomov mentions that Oxen Meadows belong to him, and Natalya and Chubukov hotly dispute the claim, drowning the marriage question in a land quarrel.
concepts.key_idea: The meadows are worth little, yet pride escalates the argument, and Lomov leaves the house with the proposal unsaid.

solution_steps.explain: Lomov claims Oxen Meadows as his, while the Chubukovs insist they have held them for generations.
Insults fly about ancestors and land grabbing, and both sides forget the proposal entirely.
Lomov storms out with palpitations, and only later does Chubukov recall that Lomov came to propose.

concepts.title: The Quarrel over the Dogs Squeezer and Guess
concepts.definition: When Lomov returns and is about to be accepted, he and Natalya quarrel again over whose dog is better: Chubukov's Squeezer or Lomov's Guess, each citing price, pedigree and performance at the dog show.
concepts.key_idea: The second argument again eclipses the proposal, and Lomov's legs go numb as he collapses in a chair with palpitations.

solution_steps.explain: Squeezer, Chubukov's dog, cost a hundred and twenty-five roubles, while Guess cost eighty-five.
Each side cites pedigree, price and the dog's showing at the trial, with insults flying.
Lomov's palpitations and numb foot end with him fainting into a chair.

concepts.title: The Hasty Marriage: The Play's Farce and Theme
concepts.definition: When Lomov recovers, Chubukov thrusts the couple's hands together and declares them engaged, and Natalya and Lomov resume bickering even as they accept, exposing marriage as a social bargain in Chekhov's farce.
concepts.key_idea: The play satirises landowners who treat marriage as a merger of property, with quarrels continuing even at the moment of engagement.
question_patterns: how does the play the proposal end
what does the quarrelsome ending say about marriage in the play
why is the proposal called a farce

do natalya and lomov love each other explain

solution_steps.explain: Chubukov puts Lomov's hand in Natalya's, kisses them, and announces the betrothal while they argue.
Marriage is treated as a practical arrangement between wealthy landowning families, not romance.
Exaggerated arguments over trifles, fainting fits and instant reversals mark the play as a farce.
